work.title: Alexander, Who Used to Be Rich Last Sunday
work.note: Alexander, Who Used to Be Rich Last Sunday é um livro infantil de Judith Viorst sobre um menino e o dinheiro que ele gasta. A referência é o livro de moedas que acabam.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Educação e tom
facts.sub: Staff often ask “How much do you want to add?” You can answer with just the amount.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: Many American cities have a reloadable card for buses and trains. You add money once, then you just tap the card and go.

compare.br: In Brazil, many cities have their own transit card (São Paulo has the Bilhete Único), and you can often recharge it at a booth or an app.
compare.us: In the USA each region has its own card, and you can often add money at a machine or online.
compare.tip: Check your balance before you travel so you do not have a problem at the reader.
compare.ask: How much money do you usually add to your card? Say it in English.

pages.title: Nina’s first transit card · 1/3
paragraphs: Nina arrived in San Francisco on Monday. She wanted to ride the bus, but she did not have a transit card. She walked to a small shop near the station and said, “**Hi! I need a transit card.**”

“**Sure. How much do you want to add?**” the clerk asked. Nina counted her money. “**Twenty dollars, please**,” she said. “**Cash or card?**” “**Cash. Here you go**,” she answered and gave him a twenty-dollar bill.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Nina’s first transit card · 2/3
paragraphs: The clerk put the card in a machine and added the money. Then he said, “**Here’s your card and your change**.” Nina looked at the change in her hand. There were a few coins because the card cost a little.
“**How do I use it?**” she asked. “**Tap it on the reader**,” he said. “It makes a small sound when it works.” Nina put the card in her bag and said, “**Have a nice day!**”

pages.title: Nina’s first transit card · 3/3
paragraphs: At the bus stop, she tapped the card on the reader. It made a short sound, and a green light came on. Nina smiled. She did not need coins, and she did not need to ask the driver for help.
Later, she told her friend, “A transit card is easy. You tap and go!” Nina felt more at home in the city.
